name: Golden Ten
description: Golden Ten is a reverse trick-taking game using a 56-card Rook deck: players avoid red-card penalties while trying to capture the yellow ten bonus card.

overview.description: Golden Ten is a reverse trick-taking game using a 56-card Rook deck: players avoid red-card penalties while trying to capture the yellow ten bonus card.

history.origins: Golden Ten is a Hearts-like reverse game adapted to the color-and-rank structure of Rook cards.
timeline: Rook era: Color-suited Rook packs inspired many non-standard trick games.
Golden Ten period: Reverse-penalty play emerged with red penalties plus yellow-ten offset.
Current play: Usually run as a fixed set of six deals.
history.cultural: It sits within social Rook-table traditions that favor low-score-wins avoidance games.
history.evolution: Core rules stay simple: plain trick-taking with follow-color obligation and no trump, then penalty scoring.

setup.deck: 56 cards: four colors (red, yellow, green, black), ranks 1 through 14.
setup.dealing: Deal all cards as equally as possible; with 3, 5, or 6 players, leftovers are won by winner of first trick.
setup.equipment: Scorepad for cumulative penalty totals across six deals.

rules.objective: Finish six deals with the lowest cumulative penalty score.
rules.gameplay: Player left of dealer leads first trick. Players must follow led color when possible; otherwise any card may be played. Highest card of led color wins the trick and leads next. There is no trump. After all cards are played, penalty points are counted from captured tricks and added to cumulative total.
keyRules: Each red card captured is 1 penalty, except red 5 is 5 and red 10 is 10.
Yellow 10 (Golden Ten) subtracts 10 from your red penalties in that deal, minimum zero.
Game length is six deals with dealer moving left each deal.
Lowest cumulative penalty after final deal wins.

strategy.basic: Avoid taking tricks that may contain red cards, especially red 10 and red 5.
strategy.intermediate: Time high yellow cards to improve chances of winning the trick that contains yellow 10.
strategy.advanced: Track remaining high cards by color to offload lead control when dangerous reds are still unplayed.
tips: Yellow 10 is most valuable when you already hold meaningful red penalties.
When void in led color, dump dangerous reds whenever safe.

variations.name: Fixed Six Deals
variations.description: Standard session consists of exactly six deals and lowest cumulative penalty wins.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Standard rules; no engine overrides needed for base game.

variations.name: Long Session Target
variations.description: Alternative table rule continues beyond six deals to an agreed round limit.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Round count would need constants.optimal_players or round_limit override when source available.

scoring.description: Each red card is 1 penalty, except red 5 is 5 and red 10 is 10. Capturing yellow 10 reduces your red penalties by 10, minimum zero.
scoring.winCondition: After six deals, player with the lowest cumulative penalty total wins.

synthesis.shortDescription: A no-trump avoidance trick game where red captures hurt and yellow ten offsets damage, scored over a fixed six-deal session.

hero.title: GOLDEN TEN
hero.subtitle: Rook Reverse Trick Game
hero.tagline: Dodge red penalties, secure yellow ten, and finish six deals with the lowest score.
